source_batch.unit_label: BFM Module D unit 3 (courseware unit 28): asset classification and provisioning norms

facts.statement: Background and NPA definition (courseware): the Narasimham Committee (1991) recommended that balance sheets be transparent and that banks adopt uniform accounting practices on income recognition and bad debt provisioning: income recognition of non-performing assets should not be on accrual basis but on record of recovery, and provisioning should depend on objective classification of assets. The central bank introduced prudential norms for income recognition, asset classification and provisioning in a phased manner from 1993 so that income recognition is objective and based on record of recovery and asset classification is on objective criteria. An asset becomes non-performing when it ceases to generate income for the bank. A non-performing asset (NPA) is a loan or advance where: interest and/or instalment of principal remains overdue for more than 90 days for a term loan; the account remains out of order for an overdraft or cash credit; the bill remains overdue for more than 90 days for bills purchased and discounted; the instalment of principal or interest remains overdue for two crop seasons for short duration crops or one crop season for long duration crops; the amount of a liquidity facility outstanding for more than 90 days in a securitisation transaction; and in derivative transactions, overdue positive mark-to-market receivables unpaid for 90 days from the due date. A bank classifies an account as NPA only if interest charged during any quarter is not serviced fully within 90 days from the end of the quarter.

Out of order and overdue (courseware): an account is out of order if the outstanding balance remains continuously in excess of the sanctioned limit or drawing power; where the outstanding balance in the principal operating account is less than the sanctioned limit or drawing power but there are no credits continuously for 90 days as on the balance sheet date, or credits are not enough to cover the interest debited during the same period, the account is also out of order. Any amount due to the bank under any credit facility is overdue if it is not paid on the due date fixed by the bank.

Income recognition and reversal (courseware): income from NPAs is not recognised on accrual basis but booked only when actually received; banks should not charge and take to income account interest on any NPA. Exception: interest on advances against term deposits, National Savings Certificates, Indira Vikas Patras, Kisan Vikas Patras and life policies may be taken to income on the due date provided adequate margin is available. Fees and commissions earned from renegotiation or rescheduling of outstanding debts are recognised on accrual basis over the period covered by the extended credit. On government guaranteed advances that become NPA, interest is not taken to income unless realised. Reversal: if any advance, including bills purchased and discounted, becomes NPA as at the close of any year, interest accrued and credited to income in the previous year should be reversed or provided for if not realised; fees, commission and similar income that accrued should cease to accrue in the current period and be reversed or provided for for past periods if uncollected. For leased assets, the finance charge component accrued and credited before the asset became non-performing and remaining unrealised is reversed or provided for. Appropriation of recovery: interest realised on NPAs may be taken to income provided the credits in the account towards interest are not out of fresh or additional credit facilities sanctioned to the same borrower; absent a clear agreement, banks apply an accounting principle of appropriating recoveries uniformly and consistently.

Categories of NPAs (courseware): banks classify NPAs into substandard, doubtful and loss assets based on the period for which the asset has remained non-performing and the realisability of the dues. A substandard asset is one that has remained NPA for a period less than or equal to 12 months; its current net worth of the borrower or guarantor or the current market value of the security is not enough to ensure recovery of dues in full; it has well-defined credit weaknesses that jeopardise liquidation of the debt, with the distinct possibility of some loss if deficiencies are not corrected. A doubtful asset is one that has remained substandard for 12 months; it has all the weaknesses of a substandard asset with the added characteristic that the weaknesses make collection or liquidation in full highly questionable and improbable. A loss asset is one where loss has been identified by the bank, internal or external auditors or the central bank inspection but the amount has not been written off wholly; it is uncollectible and of such little value that its continuance as a bankable asset is not warranted, though there may be some salvage or recovery value.

Accounts with temporary deficiencies and upgrade (courseware): classification is based on the record of recovery; an account should not be classified NPA merely because of temporary deficiencies such as non-availability of adequate drawing power based on the latest stock statement, outstanding temporarily exceeding the limit, non-submission of stock statements or non-renewal of limits on the due date. Drawing power should be based on stock statements not older than three months (older ones are irregular). A working capital account becomes NPA if there is an irregular drawing continuously for 90 days even though the unit is working or financial position is satisfactory. Regular and ad hoc credit limits should be reviewed or regularised not later than three months from the due date; delay beyond six months is not desirable and an account where limits have not been reviewed or renewed within 180 days from the due date is treated as NPA. Upgrade: if arrears of interest and principal are paid by the borrower, the account should no longer be treated as non-performing and may be classified as standard; for accounts upgraded after restructuring, specified conditions apply (satisfactory performance during a specified period for smaller MSME exposures, and for others satisfactory performance until 10 per cent of the outstanding debt is repaid). Accounts regularised near the balance sheet date should be handled with care and, where inherent weakness is evident, deemed NPA; lenders furnish evidence to the auditors.

Borrower-wise classification and special cases (courseware): asset classification is borrower-wise, not facility-wise: all facilities to a borrower and investments in all securities issued by the borrower are treated as NPA if one becomes irregular; devolved letters of credit and invoked guarantees parked in a separate account are treated as part of the borrower principal operating account for the norms; bills discounted under an LC are not classified NPA merely because the LC issuing bank fails to pay on the due date, unless the borrower does not make good the amount (other facilities to the borrower being NPA classifies them). Derivative contracts: overdue receivables representing positive mark-to-market value are treated as NPA if unpaid for 90 days; for borrower-wise classification, all funded facilities then become NPA; the accrued receivable is reversed from profit and loss to a suspense account. Consortium: classification is based on the recovery record of the individual member banks; where remittances are pooled by one bank, the account is treated as NPA if the bank receiving remittances is not parting with the shares of others. Erosion of security and frauds: where the realisable value of security is less than 50 per cent of the value assessed at the last inspection, the NPA may be classified straight away as doubtful; if less than 10 per cent of the outstanding, the existence of security is ignored and the asset is classified as loss. Fraud: banks provide for the entire amount due immediately on detection (with permitted adjustment of eligible collateral), with an option to spread over up to four quarters. Advances to primary agricultural credit societies on-lending: only the particular credit facility in default for two (or one) crop seasons becomes NPA. Loans with moratorium for payment of interest: interest becomes due only after the moratorium; housing loans to staff: NPA only on default on instalments. Agricultural advances: short duration crops overdue for two crop seasons and long duration crops (crop season longer than one year) for one crop season. Government guaranteed advances: central government guaranteed advances become NPA only when the guarantee is repudiated; state government guaranteed advances attract norms if overdue for more than 90 days. Project loans: infrastructure and non-infrastructure categories with norms for delays before commencement of commercial operations (details not taught); income on projects under implementation may be recognised on accrual if classified standard. Funded interest recognised as income must be fully provided for; conversion of interest into equity, debentures or other instruments requires full provision (not income recognition). Takeout finance, post-shipment supplier credit with a guarantee-cum-refinance cover, export project finance, securitisation transfers of assets (originating bank and purchasing bank) and credit cards (NPA if the minimum amount due is not paid within 90 days from the due date) have specific rules at the level of detail not taught.

Provisioning on NPAs (courseware): an NPA hits profitability twice: the bank stops earning interest and must provide for the asset. Loss assets are written off; if allowed to remain, 100 per cent is provided. Doubtful assets: 100 per cent of the extent to which the advance is not covered by the realisable value of security, plus provision on the secured portion at 25 per cent (doubtful up to one year), 40 per cent (one to three years) and 100 per cent (more than three years). Substandard assets: a general provision of 15 per cent on the total outstanding (without making allowance for guarantee cover and securities); unsecured exposures identified as substandard attract an additional 10 per cent (a total of 25 per cent), reduced to 20 per cent for infrastructure loan accounts with escrow safeguards; for unsecured doubtful assets, 100 per cent. Unsecured exposure means one where the realisable value of security is not more than 10 per cent ab initio of the outstanding exposure. Standard assets: general provision rates on the funded outstanding on the global loan portfolio (farm credit and small and micro enterprises 0.25 per cent; commercial real estate 1.00 per cent; commercial real estate residential housing 0.75 per cent; housing loans at teaser rates 2.00 per cent reverting to 0.40 per cent after a year; restructured advances as stipulated; other loans and advances including medium enterprises 0.40 per cent); standard asset provisions are not reckoned for arriving at net NPAs and are shown as contingent provisions in other liabilities. An unhedged foreign currency exposure of borrowers requires incremental provisions based on the likely loss to EBID (up to 15 per cent: nil; over 15 to 30 per cent: 20 basis points; over 30 to 50: 40; over 50 to 75: 60; over 75: 80). Provisioning coverage ratio (PCR) = provisions (specific plus floating) to gross NPAs; banks were asked to maintain at least 70 per cent as a macro-prudential cushion; a countercyclical provisioning buffer is segregated and used only in downturns with prior approval; PCR is disclosed in the notes to accounts. The percentages are as at the courseware date and are not taught as current.

Stress recognition and resolution (courseware): to identify incipient stress, accounts are classified as special mention accounts (SMA) before they become NPA: SMA-0 where principal or interest is not overdue for more than 30 days but the account shows signs of incipient stress (listed in the courseware table as overdue 1 to 30 days), SMA-1 overdue 31 to 60 days and SMA-2 overdue 61 to 90 days; for revolving credit facilities such as cash credit, SMA-1 is where the outstanding remains continuously in excess of the sanctioned limit or drawing power (whichever is lower) for 31 to 60 days and SMA-2 for 61 to 90 days (no SMA-0 for revolving facilities). Lenders report credit information including SMA classification to the Central Repository of Information on Large Credits (CRILC) for borrowers with aggregate exposure of Rs 5 crore and above (Rs 50 million); banks that fail to report or conceal the actual status face accelerated provisioning. The 2019 prudential framework for resolution of stressed assets: boards approve resolution policies; a resolution plan (RP) is to be initiated before default; a prima facie review within 30 days of default (review period); if a viable RP is not implemented within 180 days from the end of the review period, additional provisions of 20 per cent are required, and 15 per cent more (35 per cent total) if not implemented within 365 days from the commencement of the review period, over and above the higher of provisions held and those required by asset classification, with total provisions capped at 100 per cent. Restructuring is a concession granted by a lender for economic or legal reasons relating to the borrower financial difficulty (modification of terms, additional credit, compromise settlements with payment over three months); signs of financial difficulty include default, probable default, delisting, inadequate cash flows and non-performing status; restructured accounts are immediately downgraded to NPA (substandard as a start, keeping prior ageing for NPAs); income on restructured standard accounts is on accrual basis and on NPAs on cash basis. An accelerated provisioning table raised provisions for substandard unsecured and doubtful accounts (figures not taught).

Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code and bad bank (courseware, concepts only): the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 consolidated insolvency laws to give a time-bound resolution framework; it shifted the regime from debtor-in-possession to creditor-in-control, handing control to a committee of creditors and an insolvency professional; three classes (financial creditors, operational creditors and corporate debtors) can trigger the corporate insolvency resolution process; a moratorium follows admission of a petition; the resolution process is to be completed within a statutory period (180 days extendable, with an outer limit as amended); certain persons (for example related parties and those who contributed to the default) are barred from submitting a resolution plan or sitting on the committee of creditors; the adjudicating authority for corporates is the National Company Law Tribunal; insolvency professionals are regulated by the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India; the courseware cites workers dues and priority provisions. A bad bank is a financial entity set up to buy NPAs from banks, easing balance sheets so that banks can lend again; it may restructure and sell the assets; the courseware describes a company (NARCL) to acquire stressed assets and another (IDRCL) to manage and sell them, with a government guarantee on security receipts. Details and figures are narrative and are not taught.

payload.title: Why prudential norms exist, and what an NPA is
payload.core_explanation_md:
The **Narasimham Committee (1991)** called for **transparent balance sheets** and **objective** income recognition and provisioning: **income on NPAs on record of recovery**, not accrual, and **provisioning tied to asset classification**. The central bank introduced the norms **in phases from 1993**.

An asset becomes **non-performing** when it **stops generating income**. An **NPA** is a loan or advance where:

| Facility | NPA when |
| --- | --- |
| **Term loan** | **Interest or instalment overdue more than 90 days** |
| **Overdraft / cash credit** | Account **out of order** |
| **Bills purchased and discounted** | Bill **overdue more than 90 days** |
| **Agricultural, short duration crops** | **Overdue for two crop seasons** |
| **Agricultural, long duration crops** | **Overdue for one crop season** |
| **Securitisation liquidity facility** | Outstanding **more than 90 days** |
| **Derivatives** | Overdue **positive MTM receivable unpaid 90 days** |

Interest charged in a quarter must be **serviced fully within 90 days of quarter end**, or the account is NPA.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The 90-day rule makes classification mechanical and removes judgement from income recognition.

self_check.prompt_text: After how many days of overdue interest does a term loan become an NPA?
self_check.expected_takeaway: More than 90 days.

payload.title: Out of order and overdue
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Out of order:** the outstanding balance stays **continuously above the sanctioned limit or drawing power**. Also out of order if the balance is **within the limit** but there are **no credits continuously for 90 days** at the balance sheet date, or the credits **do not cover the interest** debited in that period.

**Overdue:** any amount due under a credit facility that is **not paid on the due date** fixed by the bank.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: A cash credit account has no instalment, so out of order status plays the role of default.

self_check.prompt_text: When is an overdraft account out of order?
self_check.expected_takeaway: When the outstanding stays continuously above the limit or drawing power, or there are no adequate credits for 90 days.

payload.title: Income recognition and reversal
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Rule:** income from an NPA is **booked only when actually received**; banks **do not charge and take to income** interest on an NPA.

**Exceptions:** interest on advances against **term deposits, NSCs, IVPs, KVPs and life policies** may be taken on the due date if **adequate margin** exists.

**Reversal:** when an advance becomes NPA at the year end, **interest accrued and credited in the previous year** is **reversed or provided for** if unrealised; **fees, commission and similar income** stop accruing and are reversed or provided for.

**Other rules:** **fees on rescheduling** are recognised **over the extended period**; **government guaranteed NPAs**: interest not taken to income **unless realised**; **leased assets**: **unrealised finance charge reversed**.

**Appropriation of recovery:** interest realised on an NPA can be taken to income **only if the credit is not from fresh or additional facilities** to the same borrower.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Taking interest to income from a loan funded by the bank itself would be evergreening.

self_check.prompt_text: Can interest on an NPA be taken to income on accrual?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No; only when actually received, apart from the exceptions for deposit-secured advances.

payload.title: Substandard, doubtful and loss assets
payload.core_explanation_md:
| Category | Definition (courseware) |
| --- | --- |
| **Substandard** | NPA for **12 months or less**; **well-defined credit weaknesses** that jeopardise recovery; **some loss possible** if not corrected |
| **Doubtful** | Remained **substandard for 12 months**; **collection in full highly questionable and improbable** |
| **Loss** | Loss **identified** by the bank, auditors or inspection but **not fully written off**; **uncollectible**, only some **salvage value** |

Classification depends on the **period as NPA** and the **realisability of dues**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: An asset moves down the ladder with the passage of time unless recovery occurs.

self_check.prompt_text: When does a substandard asset become doubtful?
self_check.expected_takeaway: When it has remained substandard for 12 months.

payload.title: Temporary deficiencies, upgrade and regularisation
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Do not classify as NPA** merely because of **temporary deficiencies**: no adequate **drawing power** on the latest stock statement, a **temporary excess**, **missing stock statements**, or **limits not renewed** on the due date.

- Drawing power uses **stock statements not older than three months**.
- A working capital account becomes NPA if **irregular drawings continue for 90 days**, even if the unit is working.
- Limits should be **reviewed within three months** of the due date; **beyond 180 days without review** the account is NPA.

**Upgrade:** when **all arrears of interest and principal are paid** the account can return to **standard**; restructured accounts need **satisfactory performance** over a stated period.

**Window dressing:** accounts regularised **near the balance sheet date** with inherent weakness are treated as NPA; lenders must give evidence to auditors.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The test is the record of recovery, not the borrower story.

self_check.prompt_text: How old may stock statements be when computing drawing power?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Not older than three months.

payload.title: Borrower-wise classification and special cases
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Classification is borrower-wise, not facility-wise:** if one facility becomes NPA, **all facilities and investments in the borrower securities** are classified NPA.

- **Devolved LCs and invoked guarantees** in a separate account count as part of the **principal operating account**.
- **Derivatives:** overdue positive MTM receivable **unpaid 90 days** is NPA; borrower-wise, other **funded facilities** follow; the accrued amount is **reversed to a suspense account**.
- **Consortium:** classification follows each member bank's **own record of recovery**; pooled remittances not shared make the account NPA in the other banks' books.
- **Erosion of security or fraud:** realisable security **below 50 per cent** of assessed value: classify **straight to doubtful**; **below 10 per cent** of outstanding: **loss**.
- **Fraud:** provide for the **whole amount** on detection (option to **spread over up to four quarters**).
- **Agricultural:** two crop seasons (short crops), one (long crops, longer than a year).
- **Government guaranteed:** central guarantee advances become NPA only when the guarantee is **repudiated**; state guarantee advances after **90 days**.
- **Moratorium:** interest is due only **after** it.
- **Funded interest** recognised as income must be **fully provided for**; **conversion of interest** to equity or debentures needs **full provision**, not income recognition.
- **Credit card:** NPA if the **minimum amount due is unpaid within 90 days** of the due date.

Project loans, takeout finance, export project finance and securitisation have specific rules at a level of detail not taught.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: A borrower in trouble on one loan is treated as in trouble on all.

self_check.prompt_text: What does borrower-wise classification mean?
self_check.expected_takeaway: If one facility to a borrower becomes NPA, all facilities to that borrower are classified as NPA.

payload.title: Provisioning norms (courseware figures)
payload.core_explanation_md:
An NPA hits profit **twice**: **interest stops** and a **provision** is needed.

| Category | Provision (courseware) |
| --- | --- |
| **Loss** | **Written off** (or **100 per cent** if it remains) |
| **Doubtful** | **100 per cent of the unsecured part** plus **25 per cent** (up to 1 year), **40 per cent** (1-3 years), **100 per cent** (over 3 years) of the **secured** part |
| **Substandard** | **15 per cent** of total outstanding; **unsecured exposures** an extra **10 per cent** (**25 per cent**), **20 per cent** for infrastructure loans with escrow |
| **Unsecured doubtful** | **100 per cent** |
| **Standard** | **0.25** (farm and small and micro), **0.40** (others), **1.00** (commercial real estate), **0.75** (CRE housing), **2.00** (housing at teaser rates, then 0.40) per cent |

**Unsecured exposure:** security realisable value **not more than 10 per cent** ab initio. **Provisioning coverage ratio (PCR) = provisions held / gross NPAs**; banks were asked to keep **at least 70 per cent**. **Standard asset provisions** are not netted when computing **net NPAs**. **Unhedged foreign currency exposure** of borrowers attracts **incremental provisions** from **20 to 80 basis points** rising with likely loss to earnings.

**The percentages are the courseware figures as at its date and are not taught as current.**
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The longer an asset stays doubtful, the higher the provision on even its secured part.

self_check.prompt_text: What does a provisioning coverage ratio measure?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Provisions held as a percentage of gross NPAs.

payload.title: Provision calculation and net NPA
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Substandard provision = rate x total outstanding.**

**Doubtful provision = 100% x unsecured portion + rate x secured portion**, where **unsecured portion = outstanding - realisable value of security**.

**Net NPA = gross NPA - provisions held on NPAs** (standard asset provisions are not deducted).

**PCR = provisions on NPAs / gross NPAs x 100.**

Example (rates as assumptions): doubtful (1-3 years), outstanding **Rs 100 lakh**, security **Rs 60 lakh**: provision **= 40 + 0.40 x 60 = Rs 64 lakh**.

variables.name: Provision rate on the secured portion

assumptions: Rates are those stated in the question
common_errors: Applying the rate to the whole outstanding
Netting standard asset provisions in net NPA

payload.expanded_explanation_md: The unsecured portion is fully provided; only the secured portion earns a lower rate.

self_check.prompt_text: How is the doubtful provision split?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Fully on the unsecured portion plus a percentage on the secured portion.

payload.title: Special mention accounts and resolution of stress
payload.core_explanation_md:
Accounts are flagged **before** they become NPA as **special mention accounts (SMA)**:

| Category | Non-revolving facilities | Revolving facilities (for example cash credit) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **SMA-0** | Overdue **1 to 30 days** (signs of incipient stress) | **Not used** |
| **SMA-1** | Overdue **31 to 60 days** | Outstanding **above limit or drawing power (lower) for 31 to 60 days** |
| **SMA-2** | Overdue **61 to 90 days** | The same excess for **61 to 90 days** |

Lenders report SMA status of larger borrowers to **CRILC**; **failure to report or concealment** brings **accelerated provisioning**.

**2019 resolution framework (courseware):** the **board approves** a resolution policy; a **resolution plan (RP)** is started **before default**; **prima facie review in 30 days** of default; if a viable RP is **not implemented within 180 days** from the end of the review period, **additional provision of 20 per cent**, **15 per cent more** (35 per cent) after **365 days**, capped so total provisions do not exceed **100 per cent**.

**Restructuring** = a concession for the borrower financial difficulty; restructured accounts are **downgraded to NPA at once** (keeping prior ageing); **income** on restructured standard accounts on **accrual**, on NPAs on **cash**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Early flags give time to resolve a stressed account before it is an NPA.

self_check.prompt_text: Which SMA categories exist for revolving credit facilities?
self_check.expected_takeaway: SMA-1 and SMA-2 only.

payload.title: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code and bad banks (concepts)
payload.core_explanation_md:
**IBC, 2016** gave a **consolidated, time-bound** insolvency framework. It moved from **debtor-in-possession** to **creditor-in-control**: a **committee of creditors** and an **insolvency professional** run the company during the **corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP)**.

- **Three classes** can trigger CIRP: **financial creditors**, **operational creditors** and **corporate debtors**.
- A **moratorium** follows admission of a petition.
- A **statutory time limit** applies (180 days, extendable, within an outer limit).
- Certain **related parties** and those linked to the default are **barred** from resolution plans and the committee.
- The **National Company Law Tribunal** adjudicates for corporates; the **Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India** regulates professionals.

**Bad bank:** an entity that **buys NPAs from banks** so they can lend again, then **restructures or sells** them; the courseware describes **NARCL** (acquires) and **IDRCL** (manages and sells) with a **government guarantee** on security receipts. Figures and rulings in the courseware are narrative and **not taught**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Creditor-in-control means the people owed money decide how the business is revived or sold.

self_check.prompt_text: Who runs the company during the corporate insolvency resolution process?
self_check.expected_takeaway: A committee of creditors with an insolvency professional, instead of the existing promoters.

items.title: Why prudential norms exist, and what an NPA is
items.core_explanation_md:
The **Narasimham Committee (1991)** called for **transparent balance sheets** and **objective** income recognition and provisioning: **income on NPAs on record of recovery**, not accrual, and **provisioning tied to asset classification**. The central bank introduced the norms **in phases from 1993**.

An asset becomes **non-performing** when it **stops generating income**. An **NPA** is a loan or advance where:

| Facility | NPA when |
| --- | --- |
| **Term loan** | **Interest or instalment overdue more than 90 days** |
| **Overdraft / cash credit** | Account **out of order** |
| **Bills purchased and discounted** | Bill **overdue more than 90 days** |
| **Agricultural, short duration crops** | **Overdue for two crop seasons** |
| **Agricultural, long duration crops** | **Overdue for one crop season** |
| **Securitisation liquidity facility** | Outstanding **more than 90 days** |
| **Derivatives** | Overdue **positive MTM receivable unpaid 90 days** |

Interest charged in a quarter must be **serviced fully within 90 days of quarter end**, or the account is NPA.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The 90-day rule makes classification mechanical and removes judgement from income recognition.

self_check.prompt_text: After how many days of overdue interest does a term loan become an NPA?
self_check.expected_takeaway: More than 90 days.

items.title: Out of order and overdue
items.core_explanation_md:
**Out of order:** the outstanding balance stays **continuously above the sanctioned limit or drawing power**. Also out of order if the balance is **within the limit** but there are **no credits continuously for 90 days** at the balance sheet date, or the credits **do not cover the interest** debited in that period.

**Overdue:** any amount due under a credit facility that is **not paid on the due date** fixed by the bank.
items.expanded_explanation_md: A cash credit account has no instalment, so out of order status plays the role of default.

self_check.prompt_text: When is an overdraft account out of order?
self_check.expected_takeaway: When the outstanding stays continuously above the limit or drawing power, or there are no adequate credits for 90 days.

items.title: Income recognition and reversal
items.core_explanation_md:
**Rule:** income from an NPA is **booked only when actually received**; banks **do not charge and take to income** interest on an NPA.

**Exceptions:** interest on advances against **term deposits, NSCs, IVPs, KVPs and life policies** may be taken on the due date if **adequate margin** exists.

**Reversal:** when an advance becomes NPA at the year end, **interest accrued and credited in the previous year** is **reversed or provided for** if unrealised; **fees, commission and similar income** stop accruing and are reversed or provided for.

**Other rules:** **fees on rescheduling** are recognised **over the extended period**; **government guaranteed NPAs**: interest not taken to income **unless realised**; **leased assets**: **unrealised finance charge reversed**.

**Appropriation of recovery:** interest realised on an NPA can be taken to income **only if the credit is not from fresh or additional facilities** to the same borrower.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Taking interest to income from a loan funded by the bank itself would be evergreening.

self_check.prompt_text: Can interest on an NPA be taken to income on accrual?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No; only when actually received, apart from the exceptions for deposit-secured advances.

items.title: Substandard, doubtful and loss assets
items.core_explanation_md:
| Category | Definition (courseware) |
| --- | --- |
| **Substandard** | NPA for **12 months or less**; **well-defined credit weaknesses** that jeopardise recovery; **some loss possible** if not corrected |
| **Doubtful** | Remained **substandard for 12 months**; **collection in full highly questionable and improbable** |
| **Loss** | Loss **identified** by the bank, auditors or inspection but **not fully written off**; **uncollectible**, only some **salvage value** |

Classification depends on the **period as NPA** and the **realisability of dues**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: An asset moves down the ladder with the passage of time unless recovery occurs.

items.title: Temporary deficiencies, upgrade and regularisation
items.core_explanation_md:
**Do not classify as NPA** merely because of **temporary deficiencies**: no adequate **drawing power** on the latest stock statement, a **temporary excess**, **missing stock statements**, or **limits not renewed** on the due date.

- Drawing power uses **stock statements not older than three months**.
- A working capital account becomes NPA if **irregular drawings continue for 90 days**, even if the unit is working.
- Limits should be **reviewed within three months** of the due date; **beyond 180 days without review** the account is NPA.

**Upgrade:** when **all arrears of interest and principal are paid** the account can return to **standard**; restructured accounts need **satisfactory performance** over a stated period.

**Window dressing:** accounts regularised **near the balance sheet date** with inherent weakness are treated as NPA; lenders must give evidence to auditors.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The test is the record of recovery, not the borrower story.

items.title: Borrower-wise classification and special cases
items.core_explanation_md:
**Classification is borrower-wise, not facility-wise:** if one facility becomes NPA, **all facilities and investments in the borrower securities** are classified NPA.

- **Devolved LCs and invoked guarantees** in a separate account count as part of the **principal operating account**.
- **Derivatives:** overdue positive MTM receivable **unpaid 90 days** is NPA; borrower-wise, other **funded facilities** follow; the accrued amount is **reversed to a suspense account**.
- **Consortium:** classification follows each member bank's **own record of recovery**; pooled remittances not shared make the account NPA in the other banks' books.
- **Erosion of security or fraud:** realisable security **below 50 per cent** of assessed value: classify **straight to doubtful**; **below 10 per cent** of outstanding: **loss**.
- **Fraud:** provide for the **whole amount** on detection (option to **spread over up to four quarters**).
- **Agricultural:** two crop seasons (short crops), one (long crops, longer than a year).
- **Government guaranteed:** central guarantee advances become NPA only when the guarantee is **repudiated**; state guarantee advances after **90 days**.
- **Moratorium:** interest is due only **after** it.
- **Funded interest** recognised as income must be **fully provided for**; **conversion of interest** to equity or debentures needs **full provision**, not income recognition.
- **Credit card:** NPA if the **minimum amount due is unpaid within 90 days** of the due date.

Project loans, takeout finance, export project finance and securitisation have specific rules at a level of detail not taught.
items.expanded_explanation_md: A borrower in trouble on one loan is treated as in trouble on all.

self_check.expected_takeaway: If one facility to a borrower becomes NPA, all facilities to that borrower are classified as NPA.

items.title: Provisioning norms (courseware figures)
items.core_explanation_md:
An NPA hits profit **twice**: **interest stops** and a **provision** is needed.

| Category | Provision (courseware) |
| --- | --- |
| **Loss** | **Written off** (or **100 per cent** if it remains) |
| **Doubtful** | **100 per cent of the unsecured part** plus **25 per cent** (up to 1 year), **40 per cent** (1-3 years), **100 per cent** (over 3 years) of the **secured** part |
| **Substandard** | **15 per cent** of total outstanding; **unsecured exposures** an extra **10 per cent** (**25 per cent**), **20 per cent** for infrastructure loans with escrow |
| **Unsecured doubtful** | **100 per cent** |
| **Standard** | **0.25** (farm and small and micro), **0.40** (others), **1.00** (commercial real estate), **0.75** (CRE housing), **2.00** (housing at teaser rates, then 0.40) per cent |

**Unsecured exposure:** security realisable value **not more than 10 per cent** ab initio. **Provisioning coverage ratio (PCR) = provisions held / gross NPAs**; banks were asked to keep **at least 70 per cent**. **Standard asset provisions** are not netted when computing **net NPAs**. **Unhedged foreign currency exposure** of borrowers attracts **incremental provisions** from **20 to 80 basis points** rising with likely loss to earnings.

**The percentages are the courseware figures as at its date and are not taught as current.**
items.expanded_explanation_md: The longer an asset stays doubtful, the higher the provision on even its secured part.

items.title: Provision calculation and net NPA
items.core_explanation_md:
**Substandard provision = rate x total outstanding.**

**Doubtful provision = 100% x unsecured portion + rate x secured portion**, where **unsecured portion = outstanding - realisable value of security**.

**Net NPA = gross NPA - provisions held on NPAs** (standard asset provisions are not deducted).

**PCR = provisions on NPAs / gross NPAs x 100.**

Example (rates as assumptions): doubtful (1-3 years), outstanding **Rs 100 lakh**, security **Rs 60 lakh**: provision **= 40 + 0.40 x 60 = Rs 64 lakh**.

items.title: Special mention accounts and resolution of stress
items.core_explanation_md:
Accounts are flagged **before** they become NPA as **special mention accounts (SMA)**:

| Category | Non-revolving facilities | Revolving facilities (for example cash credit) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **SMA-0** | Overdue **1 to 30 days** (signs of incipient stress) | **Not used** |
| **SMA-1** | Overdue **31 to 60 days** | Outstanding **above limit or drawing power (lower) for 31 to 60 days** |
| **SMA-2** | Overdue **61 to 90 days** | The same excess for **61 to 90 days** |

Lenders report SMA status of larger borrowers to **CRILC**; **failure to report or concealment** brings **accelerated provisioning**.

**2019 resolution framework (courseware):** the **board approves** a resolution policy; a **resolution plan (RP)** is started **before default**; **prima facie review in 30 days** of default; if a viable RP is **not implemented within 180 days** from the end of the review period, **additional provision of 20 per cent**, **15 per cent more** (35 per cent) after **365 days**, capped so total provisions do not exceed **100 per cent**.

**Restructuring** = a concession for the borrower financial difficulty; restructured accounts are **downgraded to NPA at once** (keeping prior ageing); **income** on restructured standard accounts on **accrual**, on NPAs on **cash**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Early flags give time to resolve a stressed account before it is an NPA.

self_check.expected_takeaway: SMA-1 and SMA-2 only.

items.title: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code and bad banks (concepts)
items.core_explanation_md:
**IBC, 2016** gave a **consolidated, time-bound** insolvency framework. It moved from **debtor-in-possession** to **creditor-in-control**: a **committee of creditors** and an **insolvency professional** run the company during the **corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP)**.

- **Three classes** can trigger CIRP: **financial creditors**, **operational creditors** and **corporate debtors**.
- A **moratorium** follows admission of a petition.
- A **statutory time limit** applies (180 days, extendable, within an outer limit).
- Certain **related parties** and those linked to the default are **barred** from resolution plans and the committee.
- The **National Company Law Tribunal** adjudicates for corporates; the **Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India** regulates professionals.

**Bad bank:** an entity that **buys NPAs from banks** so they can lend again, then **restructures or sells** them; the courseware describes **NARCL** (acquires) and **IDRCL** (manages and sells) with a **government guarantee** on security receipts.
